title: HOPS-288: A Laboratory for Complex Organics in Proto-binary/Proto-multiple Systems
question: What is the origin of complex organic molecule (COM) emission in the hierarchical proto-triple system HOPS-288, and how do COM compositions compare between its members?

recipe.goal: Measure dust continuum properties of HOPS-288-A and HOPS-288-B
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fitting on the 1.3 mm dust continuum image from the high-resolution dataset (#2018.1.01038.S)
assumptions: Source A treated as a single system since neither dataset resolves its local binarity

recipe.goal: Model circumbinary disk rotation and estimate central mass
recipe.method: Extract C18O position-velocity diagram along cut penetrating source A and B (PA = 127 deg) and fit Keplerian rotation model
key_parameters: PA = 127 deg; systemic velocity v_CBD = 5.0 km s^-1; outer radius = 1.25" (500 au)
assumptions: Keplerian rotation around a central mass M_cen; distance of 400 pc

recipe.goal: Analyze COM morphology and kinematics and derive individual stellar masses
recipe.method: Generate moment 0 maps and extract PV diagrams of CH3OH and stacked COM transitions along major axes; fit linear velocity-position relation to Keplerian rotation
key_parameters: Reference velocities: 3.5 km s^-1 (source A), 6.5 km s^-1 (source B); outer rotation radii: 200 au (0.50", source A), 40 au (0.1", source B)
assumptions: Disk mass much smaller than stellar mass; edge-on geometry; Keplerian rotation; distance = 400 pc

recipe.goal: Synthesize molecular spectra and derive excitation temperatures and column densities
recipe.method: Extract spectra at dust continuum peaks of source A and B from wide-bandwidth data (#2018.1.00302.S) and fit synthetic LTE spectra using XCLASS
key_parameters: Fixed source size = 0.37"; fixed FWHM line width = 5 km s^-1; fixed velocity offsets = 2.0 km s^-1 (source A) and 6.5 km s^-1 (source B)
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE); fixed T_ex = 200 K for species with insufficient transitions (DCN, H2S, HCCCN, and CH3OH v12=1 in source B)

recipe.goal: Compare COM column density ratios and isotopic ratios
recipe.method: Compute 12C/13C and D/H ratios of CH3OH and compare COM column density ratios between source B and source A and with literature Orion hot corinos
assumptions: ISM 12C/13C ratio of 68 adopted when deriving adjusted D/H ratios from 13CH3OH

score_reason: Both ALMA project codes are public, transitions and XCLASS fitting steps/priors are thoroughly tabulated, and numeric results are clearly reported, though some imaging and PV cut parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA data (#2018.1.01038.S and #2018.1.00302.S) with a well-specified 4-step XCLASS spectral fitting recipe and quantitative continuum, kinematic mass, and column density tables.
